commits.message:
the INPUT thesis: twelve swaps moving spend from the output side to cost reduction, treasure and a graveyard loop

Three arms in a row added a drain PAYOFF and the total did not move -- drain-v1 47.5, boss-v1
47.2, entry-v1 57.9, against a champion 59.5 and an objective of 79. entry-v1 CONFIRMED the
mechanism (noncombat damage to players 4.32 -> 10.31, interval excludes zero) and still lost
ground on the total, and the fleet control refutes the density reading: yawgmoth carries nine
drain payoffs and fires fewer of them than Edgar fires its four.

So the deck is not short of conversion. It converts: eminence mints 8.04 tokens a game, 9.64
creatures die, and the payoffs that exist fire 1.90 times. It is short of INPUT -- 5.5 attacks
a game, a biggest hit of 8.4, and the pilot's own report of sitting on one or two cards from
turn eight trying to rebuild. Twelve slots move from the output side to the input side:

  COST REDUCTION    Urza's Incubator, Bontu's Monument, Oketra's Monument -- {2} and two {1}s
                    off Vampire and creature spells, so a turn casts two vampires not one.
                    Both Monuments also carry a TRIGGER (a drain, a token), which is the
                    multiplicative shape the pilot will accept from a static permanent; a
                    flat +1/+1 anthem is not.
  MANA              Pitiless Plunderer (a Treasure per other death, at 9.64 deaths a game),
                    Black Market Connections (Treasure + card + 3/2 body, every turn).
  RECURSION         Phyrexian Reclamation returns a creature TO HAND -- eminence triggers on
                    CAST, so a reanimation straight to the battlefield mints nothing and a
                    return to hand mints a token on the recast. Stitcher's Supplier fills the
                    yard the loop spends; Qarsi Revenant reanimates on its own death.
  CONVERSION        Zulaport Cutthroat (death side) and Corpse Knight (entry side) each drain
                    one per creature, which eminence tokens trigger on both ends.
  THREAT            Falkenrath Aristocrat, 4/1 flying haste with a sacrifice outlet that has a
                    visible board payoff; Marshland Bloodcaster casts Vampires for FREE off
                    three Blood, the ceiling of the thesis.

Two of the twelve cuts are MEASURED rather than judged: Ashnod's Altar is 0 for 59 castings
under both AI profiles because colourless mana is a benefit Forge's evaluator cannot price,
and Altar of Dementia is an AI:RemoveDeck:All card cast 0 times in 860 games. Four more are
the flat-anthem shape the pilot ruled out (Patchwork Banner, Legion Lieutenant, Cordial
Vampire, Blade of the Bloodchief).

Objective forge.life_removed_total >= 79 @standard-v3, against a champion 59.535 over 144
decided games. The branch is NOT cast-checked yet and NOT measured; the arm waits on a
champion re-baseline at the new patch set.

restore Cordial Vampire: of the four each-body pumps this branch cut, it is the one that SCALES

Correcting my own misclassification before the arm spends five hours on it. I cut Cordial
Vampire describing it as 'the flat-growth shape the pilot ruled out'. Its actual text is
'whenever this creature or another creature dies, put a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire you
control' — it RE-APPLIES, on the deck's most abundant event. The deck averages 9.64 creature
deaths a game. That is the multiplies-or-scales exception the pilot named, not the flat anthem
they banned, and the distinction is the whole of their rule.

MEASURED against the fleet rather than argued: the champion carries NINE persistent each-body
pumps. treasury-v1 cut four of them, and Cordial Vampire was the only one of the four that
scales — Legion Lieutenant is a flat lord, Patchwork Banner a flat artifact anthem, and
Vampire Socialite a one-shot ETB ('when this creature enters, if an opponent lost life this
turn'). Those three cuts stand. This one did not.

It matters because the one measured precedent for cutting this layer is the go-wide refactor
that cut every lord: combat damage fell 29.07 to 18.20 and the arm read 31/400 against the
champion's 50/400, an interval excluding zero. A branch that quietly repeats the shape of a
400-game loss is worth one more look before it runs.

Oketra's Monument pays for the slot. It was the THIRD generic cost reducer in a package whose
first two already do that job, and the deck's shortage is COLOURED — black 32 sources against
a 36 target, red 20 against 22 — which a third generic {1}-off does not touch. Thirteen swaps
now, and the input thesis is unchanged: the reducers, the treasure, the graveyard loop and the
two each-creature drains are all still in.

Also worth recording: the branch does NOT lose three-colour fixing. Patchwork Banner's
`{T}: add one mana of any color` leaves, and Pitiless Plunderer's Treasures arrive, which are
any-colour and recur on every other creature's death rather than once a turn.

treasury-v1: Mirkwood Bats in, Marshland Bloodcaster out — the token event nothing else in the 99 keys on

THE PILOT SPOTTED THE CLUSTER AND THE CLUSTER'S NEW COLUMN SPOTTED THIS. Mirkwood Bats is
'Flying. Whenever you create OR SACRIFICE a token, each opponent loses 1 life'. It keys on the
TOKEN rather than on a creature entering, which is exactly why no creature-entry pattern covered
it and the scanner's first pass classed it as having no trigger at all. FIVE cards in the whole
34,084-card corpus carry that event. Edgar mints 8.04 tokens a game and the sacrifice engine
spends them freely — Falkenrath Aristocrat activated 130 times and Vish Kal 141 in 120 games —
so this fires on both ends of a token's life.

NOT A DUPLICATE, and the new column is how we know rather than guess: function_overlap reads 0.89
to Sanctum Seeker, under the 0.95 line, and nothing else in the 99 keys on `token_created` or
`sacrifice_event`. Contrast Zulaport Cutthroat, which the same column reads at 0.9801 to Blood
Artist on the SAME event — the slot that should never have been staged.

CAVEAT, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: it is a Bat. Casting it does not trigger eminence.
It multiplies the army without joining it, which is the right job for a four-drop here but is not
the cheap-Vampire-body layer.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE CORPUS BEFORE STAGING — the step skipped last time, which cost three slots:
{3}{B}, mana value 4, mono-black and so inside Mardu, commander-legal, not a Game Changer, EDHREC
rank 228, no AI:RemoveDeck flag.

MARSHLAND BLOODCASTER IS THE CUT, on both counts. I described it as a Blood-token engine that
casts Vampires for free and it is nothing of the kind — 'Flying. {1}{B}, {T}: rather than pay the
mana cost of the next spell you cast this turn, you may pay life equal to its mana value'. I had
conflated it with Voldaren Bloodcaster // Bloodbat Summoner. And the killed arm measured it inert
independently of my error: CAST 26 times across 120 games, ACTIVATED ZERO.

Fourteen staged swaps, eleven net. NOT cast-checked: the A/A is running and a shell would add
load to the one measurement whose entire purpose is to quantify this harness's noise. The
cast-check is queued behind it, and `simulate` refuses the arm until it passes.

A FLAT ANTHEM FOR A DISCOUNT PLUS A DRAIN. The Banner gives +1/+1 and a tap-for-mana the deck rarely needs; the Monument takes {1} off every creature spell AND drains each opponent for 1 whenever a creature enters -- which with eminence minting a token per other Vampire cast is two drains per cast, not one. Multiplicative, which is the only kind of static effect this deck wants.

An equipment that needs a creature to carry it and a death to grow, for a second {1}-off on every creature spell plus a 1/1 Warrior token on every nonartifact creature cast. The token is a BODY and a death, which the sacrifice side converts.

A four-drop that needs {1} and a life payment per counter, for a three-mode enchantment that makes a Treasure, draws a card, AND makes a 3/2 Rat every turn for life. Every mode is on the thesis: mana, cards, bodies. The life cost is a resource this deck regenerates.

MEASURED: the Altar is an AI:RemoveDeck:All card, cast 0 times in 860 games. The Reclamation returns a creature from the graveyard TO HAND for {1} and 2 life -- to HAND, so recasting it triggers eminence again. Cast-checked under this harness: cast 3 of 4 drawn games, activated once.

A one-mana 1/1 lifelink token that needs three attackers to flip, for a one-mana 1/1 that mills three on entry AND three on death. It FILLS the graveyard the recursion engine spends, and it is itself a cheap body that dies.

A two-drop that puts +1/+1 counters on other Vampires when something dies -- the flat-growth shape the pilot ruled out -- for a two-drop that drains each opponent for 1 when ANY creature of ours dies. At 9.64 deaths a game this is the conversion rate the deck is short of, and it is damage that does not need an attack.

A lord giving other Vampires +1/+1, for a two-drop draining each opponent for 1 on every creature ENTERING. Eminence tokens trigger it; so does every vampire cast. Entry-side conversion to pair with the Cutthroat's death-side.

A six-drop 2/2 that grows by one per discard and needs to connect, for a four-drop 4/1 FLYING HASTE that sacrifices a creature to become indestructible and grow. Haste means it attacks the turn it lands, flying means the 8.4 biggest hit is not blocked, and the sacrifice is an outlet with a visible board payoff -- the shape the AI actually activates.

A six-drop granting evasion and a draw-on-death, for a five-drop that makes a BLOOD token on every other Vampire entering and casts Vampires for free off three Blood. Free vampire casts are eminence triggers that cost nothing, which is the ceiling of the input thesis.

A three-drop that needs a Vampire to have dealt damage before it does anything, for a three-drop 3/4 FLYING DEATHTOUCH with lifelink that exiles a creature from a graveyard on entry, and whose own death puts a creature from any graveyard into play. A body, evasion, graveyard interaction and a free reanimation on one card.
